thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P1 - elevated 5xx rate for tool/function-calls in Aurora VPC (tenant: aurora-inc). Affected: dedicated pool aurora-dp-3. Error signature: fncall_parser_error / json_schema_mismatch. Paging oncall.

sam.g: Acked. I’m oncall. Pulling logs.

maya: Seeing spikes starting 11:02 UTC. Errors are JSON parse failures inside our toolcall parser: 
```
ERROR fncall_parser - schema mismatch: expected field 'user_id' (string) got object
stack: parse->validate->serialize
```
~23% of toolcall traffic for aurora is failing, higher for long prompts. No CPU/GPU pressure.

kevin: Is this limited to aurora VPC or hitting other dedicated pools? Any recent deploys?

maya: Only aurora-dp-3. No infra deploys. There was a model config push yesterday that included a parser tweak (strict_schema=true) rolled to dedicated pools 02:00 UTC.

sam.g: Hypothesis: strict_schema flip caused schema drift with aurora's tool outputs. Immediate mitigation: switch aurora route to lenient parser variant and enable fallback to hosted parser. Plan:
- set routing policy for tenant aurora-inc -> parser=legacy-lenient (canary 10% -> 100%)
- enable hosted fallback for toolcall errors
- notify CS

kevin: Sounds good. Can you run the routing change? Add a short canary first.

sam.g: Running:
```
# route override
redwoodctl routes apply --tenant aurora-inc --key parser --value legacy-lenient --canary 10
``` 
ops-bot: deploy accepted, applying canary to aurora-dp-3 (10%).

maya: Metrics: error rate dropped from 23% -> 7% on canary buckets within 60s. Good sign.

alek: Recommend also forcing KV-cache bypass for aurora for 15m in case stale cache fragments cause schema mismatch:
```
service-config set aurora-inc kv_cache.enabled=false --ttl 900
``` 
And prepare parser rollback patch (revert strict_schema change) for the model family. I’ll draft the PR.

sam.g: Applied KV bypass. ops-bot: kv_cache toggle success.

kevin: CS, can we tell customer we have a mitigaiton and see if their ops can avoid sending new schema variants for now?

tara-cs: Notified Aurora ops at 11:18 UTC: "We observed intermittent toolcall failures; we've routed you to a lenient parser and disabled cache. We expect reduced errors; engineers are rolling a fix. Will update in 30m." Customer acknowledged. :thumbsup:

maya: After full roll to 100% legacy-lenient (11:25 UTC) error rate down to 1.3% overall. Requesting we keep lenient mode + kv bypass for 1 hour while we validate.

alek: PR ready to revert strict_schema: https://git.internal/redwood/parser-reverts/pull/42 - contains unit tests and a quick compatibility shim. I can deploy a canary to aurora-dp-3 once approved.

sam.g: Approving canary deploy. ops-bot: canary deploy parser-revert to aurora-dp-3 starting.

ops-bot: canary succeed (5%) -> 50% -> 100% over 12m. No regression observed. Post-deploy metrics show errors back to baseline ~0.2%.

tara-cs: Updated Aurora: "We rolled back a parser change and applied a temporary lenient mode; your calls should be healthy now. Please reopen if you see issues." Customer replied: "Thanks, saw immediate improvement." :white_check_mark:

kevin: Good. Next steps: write tight postmortem, include timeline, impact (23% fail rate for ~23m across aurora-dp-3, EST 11:02-11:25 UTC), root cause (strict_schema toggle + unexpected tool output shape from customer workload). Actions: add safer rollout gating for parser flags, automated schema-canary tests against VPC sample traces, and an alert for sudden spike in parser_error rate per-tenant.

sam.g: Handoff to alek for postmortem and follow-ups. I’ll stay available until 12:30 UTC. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. :eyes:

alek: Taking postmortem ownership. Will schedule follow-up with CS and product to tighten rollout controls.

incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigated. Recording incident start=1783007890 end=1783008410 severity=P1 tags=[vpc,dedicated,toolcall,parser]

sam.g: closing thread for now. If anything else from aurora appears ping me. :lock:
notes: P1 paging, oncall coordination, canary routing, kv-cache bypass, parser rollback, customer notification
